turns.text: Welcome back to Field Notes. Could you start by introducing yourself to our listeners?

Thanks for having me. I'm Hana Lindqvist, and I grew up in Tromsø, right up in the north of Norway. I trained as a marine engineer at the university in Trondheim, and spent my first few years designing cooling systems for fishing boats.
How did you get from cooling systems on boats to starting a company?

A consulting job took me to Kisumu, in Kenya, and I watched fishermen on Lake Victoria lose about a third of their catch before it ever reached a market. That's what started Coldwake, which I founded in 2019. We built solar-powered cold boxes that a whole fishing co-op could share.
And how big did Coldwake grow?

By the end we had 340 units installed around Lake Victoria, across Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. The co-ops paid per kilo stored instead of buying the boxes, and that was the part that really worked. Spoilage for our members fell from around thirty percent to under eight.
Then you sold the company. What was that like?

In 2024 we sold Coldwake to Van Rijn Logistics, a Dutch logistics group. It was the right home for it, because they had the trucks and the warehouses we never would. I stayed for a year to hand things over, and then I stepped away.
So what are you working on now?

I'm back in Norway, converting small car ferries in the Lofoten islands from diesel to battery power. There are three ferries in the project, and the first one should be carrying passengers in spring 2027. The batteries are the easy part; charging at piers with a weak grid connection is the hard part.
Is that a startup, or more of a public project?

It's a joint project with the county, which owns the ferries. My small team designs the systems and the county pays for the shipyard work. It's slower than a startup, but the money is there for as long as the work takes.
You've said before that hardware founders are funded the wrong way. What do you mean by that?

Most venture funds want an exit within five to seven years, and hardware that touches the physical world takes longer than that. 从建筑设计到种咖啡，跨度挺大的。当时为什么决定回去？
我家一直种咖啡，但那时候豆子都按最低价卖给收购商，很多邻居干脆把咖啡树砍了改种茶。2018年，我和几户亲戚一起创立了云岭咖啡合作社，想把加工和销售掌握在自己手里。
合作社现在发展到什么规模了？
现在有120户农户加入，种植面积大概三千亩。我们的收购价比市场价高三成，条件是大家按统一标准采摘，只摘红透的果子。第一年很多人不信，后来看到账上的钱，才慢慢跟进来。
收购价高三成，合作社自己靠什么赚钱呢？
主要靠精品豆的溢价。我们把豆子直接卖给上海、成都的独立咖啡馆，跳过了中间好几层贸易商。每年还会拿出一部分利润，给农户做技术培训。
听说你最近在忙一个新项目？

这个中心的钱是从哪里来的？
一半是合作社这几年攒下的积累，另一半是县里的乡村振兴资金。设计是我自己做的，总算把老本行用上了。
最后想问问，你怎么看现在想回乡创业的年轻人？
我觉得回乡不是一个浪漫的选择。我的看法是，至少要准备好三年没有收入，因为农业的周期就是这么长，一季没做好就得再等一年。如果只是想逃离城市，那最好再想一想。
谢谢嘉禾，今天聊得很有收获。
谢谢你的邀请。

turns.text: Right, let's start. Two things to settle today for the customer workshop: the date, and how many people we take.
I've checked the calendar. What about the 11th of March? It's two weeks after the spring release and before the Easter holidays.
That works on my side, Lena. Nothing else is booked that week.
Fine, let's do that.
Then numbers. The big room at the Mill seats 60, but last year it felt crowded with 55 people in it.
I'd keep it smaller so people actually talk to each other. Let's cap it at 40.
Agreed, 40 feels right. Everyone gets a seat at a table that way.
One thing from last year's survey: the main complaint was that the afternoon sessions ran too long.
That's useful, thanks Tom. So it's the 11th of March, with a cap of 40 people.
Yes, that's it.
Sam, can you book the big room at the Mill?
Sure, I'll book it by the 20th of November and send the confirmation round to everyone.
Great, thanks all.

turns.text: Hi all, thanks for making the time. This is about the annual report print run. Who have I got on the line?

Hannah here, I'm your account manager. I've got our paper buyer and our press scheduler on the call too. Just so we start from the same numbers, the quote you have right now is £3,950 for 1,200 copies, all on the coated stock.
Great. A question for the paper side, then: what does the coated stock do to the weight? Our mailing house priced the postage for anything under 250 grams a copy.
On the coated stock, each copy comes out at about 340 grams. I weighed a blank dummy this morning.
Ah, that's well over. So what would you swap it for? I don't want it looking cheap.

I'd go with a lighter uncoated paper for the inside pages and keep the coated just for the cover. That brings it to roughly 230 grams, and we've got the uncoated in stock, so your press date doesn't move.
That sounds right. Let's go with uncoated inside and coated for the cover. Hannah, can you redo the quote on that basis?
Sure, it should come down a little. I'll send you the revised quote by Wednesday the 11th.
Lovely. And the hard proof, is that coming from scheduling?
Yes, that's me. I'll courier a hard proof to your office by Monday the 16th.
Perfect. On our end, I'll get the board to sign off the proof and send you the approval by Thursday the 19th.
Hannah again. That timing works for us, so we'll keep your press slot as it is.
Brilliant. Thanks, all three of you.
Thanks, speak soon.
喂，大家好。今天主要是把我们公司年底体检的事儿对一下，你们那边人都到齐了吧？
到齐了到齐了。我是孙悦，你们这单一直是我在跟。我把排期的同事和我们体检科的同事也拉进来了。先把数对一下哈，按 120 个人算，基础套餐一个人 560。
好的。那我先问下体检科这边，我们好多同事想加个甲状腺彩超，单加的话大概多少钱？
可以加的，甲状腺彩超单加一个人多 150。
嗯，这个还能接受。还有个事儿，上回我们去的那家，一大早排了快俩小时的队，大家意见特别大。排期这边有没有什么办法？
这个好办。我建议你们分两天来，每天上午来六十个人左右，基本就不用怎么排队了。
行，这个好，那就分两天来。孙经理，加了甲状腺这项，合同是不是得重新出一版？
对，我这边改一下，周三，就是 11 号之前，把新合同发您。
好嘞。那预约链接是排期这边发是吧？
对，我来发。周五 13 号之前我把两天的预约链接发给您，您转给同事让他们自己选时间就行。
OK。那我这边下周二，17 号之前，把参加体检的员工名单整理好发给你们。
我孙悦再补一句啊，名单里麻烦把性别和身份证号都带上，我们得提前录系统。
好，没问题，我一块儿整理。那今天就先这样，辛苦各位了。
好的好的，拜拜。
